How to make a QR code for a business card

A vCard is the standard file format for contact information, and a vCard QR code is that file stored inside the pattern.

  1. Enter your first and last name. Add your company, job title, phone, email and website if you want them saved.
  2. Check every field. A typo ends up in other people's contacts.
  3. Choose colors and a style. A dark code on a light background scans best.
  4. Download the SVG for print or a high-resolution PNG.
  5. Place it on your card, then scan the printed card with two phones to test.

vCard code or link on a business card?

You can put either on a card. They suit different goals.

vCard (contact details)Link (website or profile)
What happens on scanThe phone offers to save you as a contactA page opens in the browser
Best forBeing found and called: sales, trades, consultants, agentsShowing work: portfolios, creators, online presence
Works without internetYes, the data is in the codeNo
Can you change it laterNo, it is staticOnly by changing the page it points to
DensityDenser, needs a larger print sizeSimpler, easier to scan small

What to put in the vCard

More fields make a denser code, and a denser code needs more room on a small card.

  • Always: name and one way to reach you, usually a mobile number or an email.
  • Usually: company and job title, so people remember who you are.
  • Optional: website. A short address keeps the code simple.
  • Think twice about: home address and private numbers. A vCard shows everything in plain form to anyone who scans it.

Size and placement on the card

The most common mistake is a code too small for its content.

  • Size: at least 2 cm (0.8 in) square, and about 2.5 cm (1 in) is a safer choice. A vCard with many fields may need more. Read the QR code size guide.
  • Position: the back of the card is popular because it leaves a clean area for the margin and a call to action.
  • Quiet zone: keep a blank margin of at least four modules around the code.
  • Contrast: dark code on a light background, and avoid glossy varnish on the code area.
  • Call to action: a short line like "Scan to save my contact" makes people use it.

How it behaves on different phones

Current iPhones and Android phones read a vCard code with the camera and offer to save the contact, though the wording and steps differ. This tool writes vCard version 3.0, which is widely supported. Some phones and apps show fewer fields than others, so test on the phones your contacts are likely to use.

Privacy

A vCard QR code contains your details in readable form. Only include what you are happy for anyone who gets your card to have. The code is created in your browser, and what you type is not sent to our servers.
